I, 8.],” that is, the imitation of Christ’s action beneath the flight of their contemplation. A hand, God’s power, as in Ezekiel: “The hand of the Lord came upon me [Note: [Col. 0993] 28 Ezek. XXXVII, 1; XL, 1.],” that is, the Lord’s power was revealed to me. A hand, the power of Antichrist, as in Daniel: “Deceit will be directed by his hand [Note: [Col. 0993] 29 Dan. VIII, 25.],” that is, deception will be exercised through the power of Antichrist. A hand, the devil’s temptation, as in Job: “Behold, he is in your hand [Note: [Col. 0993] 30 Job II, 6.],” that is, you have permission to tempt him. A hand, daily persecution, as in Job: “Remove your hand far from me [Note: [Col. 0993] 31 Job XIII, 21.],” that is, remove your persecution from me for a little while. A hand, the Jewish people, as in the Psalms: “Why do you turn away your hand [Note: [Col. 0993] 32 Ps. LXXIII, 11.]?” that is, why do you cast the Jewish people away from you? A hand, the persecution of the Jews, as in Job: “Place me beside you, and let anyone’s hand fight against me [Note: [Col. 0993] 33 Job XVII, 3.],” that is, when I sit at your right hand, the persecution of the Jews will not be able to touch me. A hand, an intimate friend, as in the Gospel: “If your hand causes you to stumble [Note: [Col. 0993] 34 Matt. V, 31; XVIII, 8; Mark IX, 43.],” that is, if your necessary friend urges you to sin. A hand, the enemy’s cunning, as in the Song of Exodus: “My hand will kill them [Note: [Col. 0993] 35 Exod. XV, 9.],” that is, through consent to what is unlawful the ancient enemy’s cunning will hand them over, which is said to be in it [lacuna], because it is permitted in order to deceive. By hand, many actions, as in the Psalms: “He teaches my hands for battle [Note: [Col. 0993] 36 Ps. XVII, 35; CXLIII, 1.],” that is, my works, so that they may resist iniquity. By hands, martyrs, as in the Song: “My hands dripped with myrrh [Note: [Col. 0993] 37 Song V, 5.],” that is, my martyrs did not cease until death. By hands, good workers, as in the Song: * “His hands are rounded works, * of gold [Note: [Col. 0993] 38 Ibid., v. 14.],” because good workers shine in charity without error. By hand, discernment, as in the Gospel: “The disciples were rubbing ears of grain with their hands [Note: [Col. 0993] 39 Luke VI, 1.],” because in the sayings of Scripture teachers seek spiritual understanding through the effort of discernment. By hand, God’s dispositions, as in the Psalms: “In your hands are my lots [Note: [Col. 0995] 1 Ps. XXX, 15.],” that is, my outcomes are in your dispositions. By hands, spiritual cares, as in the Psalms: “My soul is always in my hands [Note: [Col. 0995] 2 Ps. CXVIII, 109.],” [that is,] I will continually devote myself to the spiritual cares of my soul. By hand, * [lacuna] of God, as in the Psalms: “Into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit [Note: [Col. 0995] 3 Ps. XXX, 6.].”

Manna is Christ’s body, as in the Psalms: “He gave them manna to eat [Note: [Col. 0995] 4 Ps. LXXVII, 24.],” because in the desert of the present life we have Christ’s body [lacuna]. Manna, sacred Scripture, as in the Book of Numbers: “The manna was like coriander seed [Note: [Col. 0995] 5 Num. XI, 7.],” because sacred Scripture contains spiritual understanding within itself. Manna, heavenly blessedness, as in the Apocalypse: “To the one who conquers I will give hidden manna [Note: [Col. 0995] 6 Apoc. II, 17.],” because whoever perseveres to the end [Col. 0995B] will possess “what eye has not seen, what ear has not heard, what has not entered the human heart [Note: [Col. 0995] 7 Isa. LXIV, 4; I Cor. II, 9.].”

Sheaves are good works, as in Genesis: “Your sheaves stood around and worshiped my sheaf [Note: [Col. 0995] 8 Gen. XXXVII, 7.],” because holy men know that they cannot be compared with Christ on account of their works, however good they may be. Sheaves, the rewards of the saints, as in the Psalms: “Carrying their sheaves [Note: [Col. 0995] 9 Ps. CXXV, 6.],” because on account of the seeds of good works that they now possess, they will receive eternal rewards at the end.

Mandrakes are good reputation, as in the Song: “The mandrakes gave forth their fragrance at our gates” [Note: [Col. 0995] 10 Song 7:13]; that is, persons of good reputation have brought renown into your churches. Mandrakes, popular glory, as in Genesis: “Give me a share of the mandrakes” [Note: [Col. 0995] 11 Gen. 30:14], that is, of popular praise.

A border is faith, as in Ezekiel: “And the border before the chamber” [Note: [Col. 0995] 12 Ezek. 40:12], that is, faith before contemplation.

The sea is baptism, as in the Apocalypse: “A glassy sea like crystal” [Note: [Col. 0995] 13 Rev. 4:6], that is, baptism possessing purity and firmness of faith. The sea, the world, as in Job: “Who walks upon the waves of the sea?” [Note: [Col. 0995] 14 Job 9:8], that is, he who overcomes [lacuna] of the world. The sea, the Gentiles, as in the Psalms: “The mountains shall be moved into the heart of the sea” [Note: [Col. 0995] 15 Ps. 45:3], that is, the apostles shall be converted to the Gentiles. The sea, wicked people, as in the Psalms: “You created the north and the sea” [Note: [Col. 0995] 16 Ps. 89:13], that is, you formed the devil [lacuna] into members as punishments. The sea, secular occupation, as in the Psalms: “Those who go down to the sea in ships” [Note: [Col. 0995] 17 Ps. 107:23], because prelates, in governing the churches, involve themselves in managing secular affairs. The sea, hell, as in Job: “Have you entered into the depths of the sea?” [Note: [Col. 0995] 18 Job 38:16], because Christ descended into hell. The sea, the pleasure of worldly people, as in Job: “He will make the deep boil like a pot” [Note: [Col. 0995] 19 Job 41:22], because the devil sets a wicked mind on fire through unlawful desires. The sea, the punishment of Gehenna, as in the Song of Exodus: “And the sea covered them,” that is, the punishment of hell overwhelmed them [Note: [Col. 0995] 20 Exod. 15:10].

Marble is good firmness, as in the Song: “His legs are like marble columns” [Note: [Col. 0995] 21 Song 5:15], because those who support Christ in his members are firm and steadfast.

A pearl is heavenly desire, as in the Gospel: “Having found one precious pearl” [Note: [Col. 0995] 22 Matt. 13:46], that is, when a heavenly desire has been conceived in the mind. Pearls signify spiritual sacraments, as in the Gospel: “Do not cast your pearls before swine” [Note: [Col. 0995] 23 Matt. 7:6], that is, do not entrust inner mysteries to the unclean. Pearls signify righteous people, as in the Apocalypse: “Twelve pearls, twelve gates” [Note: [Col. 0995] 24 Rev. 21:21], because holy people, through the faith of the apostles, provide access to the heavenly kingdom. Pearls signify earthly delights, as in the Apocalypse: “The woman was adorned with pearls” [Note: [Col. 0995] 25 Rev. 17:4], because the deception of this age shines with earthly delights.

A male is the spirit of a human being, as in Genesis: “He made them male and female” [Note: [Col. 0995] 26 Gen. 1:27 and 5:2]; for, as John Chrysostom says, a human being is nothing other than the union of body and soul [the supplied text is corrupt here]. A male, any human being, as in Genesis: “The male whose flesh has not been circumcised” [Note: [Col. 0995] 27 Gen. 17:14], because every person who does not cut away unlawful acts will perish. A male, the rational sense of the soul, as in Exodus: “If it is a male, kill it” [Note: [Col. 0995] 28 Exod. 1:16], because the devil strives to extinguish the rational sense in a human being.

A mother is a city, as in Paul: “The Jerusalem above is free, which is our mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 29 Gal. 4:26], because no one is subject to the slavery of sin. That city is heavenly. A mother, the holy Church, as in Proverbs: “Who despises the birth of his mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 30 Prov. 30:16], that is, whoever disdains the growth of the holy Church. A mother, the Virgin Mary, as in the Song: “Look upon King Solomon with the diadem with which his mother crowned him” [Note: [Col. 0995] 31 Song 3:11], that is, love Christ in the humanity with which the Virgin Mary clothed him. A mother, the grace of God, as in the Song: “My dove, my undefiled one, is one to her mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 32 Song 6:8], because the grace of God causes unity to exist through the simplicity of the holy Church. A mother, corrupted nature, as in Job: “I said to corruption: You are my mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 33 Job 17:14], because through sin human nature is reduced to corruption. A mother, the Jewish people who crucified Christ, as in the Song: “There the mother was corrupted” [Note: [Col. 0995] 34 Song 8:5], because, when the Jewish people fastened Christ to the cross, it fell into spiritual corruption. A mother, the Synagogue, as in the Song: “I held him and will not let him go until I bring him into the house of his mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 35 Song 3:4], because now the faith of Christ is held in the Church, and the Synagogue receives it at the end of the world. A mother, every preacher, as in the Gospel: “He himself is my brother and sister and mother” [Note: [Col. 0995] 36 Matt. 12:50; Mark 3:35; Luke 8:21], because by teaching others the preacher gives birth to them in faith. A mother, concupiscence, as in the Psalms: “From my mother’s womb you are my protector” [Note: [Col. 0997] 1 Ps. 70:6; Ps. 21:11], that is, you protected me from the womb of concupiscence. A mother, the first mother Eve, as in the Psalms: “My father and my mother have forsaken me,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0997] 2 Ps. 26:10], that is, Adam and Eve exposed me to sin, and Christ redeemed me. A mother, the earth, as in Ecclesiasticus: “Until the day of return to the mother of all” [Note: [Col. 0997] 3 Sir. 40:1], that is, to the earth, which receives everyone into itself.

A hammer is the devil, as in Jeremiah: “The hammer of the whole earth has been shattered” [Note: [Col. 0997] 4 Jer. 50:23], that is, the devil has been conquered—the one who shattered sinners. A hammer, heavenly striking, as in Job: “He will regard the hammer as straw” [Note: [Col. 0997] 5 Job 41:20], because the body of the devil, which is the mass of the reprobate, does not fear heavenly striking.

A jaw is the Church, as in Job: “They struck my cheek” [Note: [Col. 0997] 6 Job 16:10], that is, they oppressed my Church. A jaw, preaching, as in the book of Judges: “With the jawbone of an ass I struck them” [Note: [Col. 0997] 7 Judg. 15:16], because through the simple teaching of the apostles he cast down the proud. A jaw, the malice of the devil, as in Job: “The jaw of Leviathan is pierced with a hook” [Note: [Col. 0997] 8 Job 40:21], because God, through his presence, freed us from the devil’s malice.

Marrow is the body of Christ, as in the song of Deuteronomy: “And goats with the marrow of wheat” [Note: [Col. 0997] 9 Deut. 32:14], that is, works of repentance together with the work of Christ. Marrow signifies earthly riches, as in Job: “And his bones are moistened with marrow” [Note: [Col. 0997] 10 Job 21:24], because impious men are sustained by earthly riches. Marrows signify intentions, as in Paul: “Of joints also and marrow” [Note: [Col. 0997] 11 Heb. 4:12], that is, of thoughts and intentions.

Honey is divinity itself, as in Job: “A torrent of honey and butter” [Note: [Col. 0997] 12 Job 20:17], and [of] the abundance of calamity and humanity [the supplied text is corrupt]. Honey, spiritual wisdom, as in Proverbs: “You have found honey; eat what is sufficient for you” [Note: [Col. 0997] 13 Prov. 25:16], that is, do not be wise beyond what is fitting. Honey, contemplation, as in the Song: “Honey and milk are under your tongue” [Note: [Col. 0997] 14 Song 4:11], because preachers teach both contemplation and action. Honey, holy souls, as in the Song: “I ate my honeycomb with my honey” [Note: [Col. 0997] 15 Song 5:1], that is, I shall unite holy souls, rejoicing in the immortality of the flesh, to myself. Honey, the sweetness of the flesh, as in the Law: “Nothing leavened or honey shall be burned in the sacrifice of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0997] 16 Lev. 2:11], because neither pride of mind nor pleasure of the flesh pleases him. Honey, the teaching of Christ, as in the song of Deuteronomy: “They sucked honey from the rock” [Note: [Col. 0997] 17 Deut. 32:13], that is, they received sweet teaching from Christ.

Members are the young and tender in the Church, as in Job: “My members have been reduced almost to nothing” [Note: [Col. 0997] 18 Job 17:7], that is, my tender and weak members have almost been consumed. Members, the reprobate, as in Job: “The members of his flesh cling together” [Note: [Col. 0997] 19 Job 41:14], and agree with one another in evil.

Months are the limits of actions, as in Job: “I have had months of emptiness” [Note: [Col. 0997] 20 Job 7:3], that is, emptiness at the limits of my actions. Months, the orders of angels, as in Job: “Let it not be counted among the months of the year” [Note: [Col. 0997] 21 Job 3:6], that is, the diabolical spirit does not attain salvation among the elect angels. A month, good rest of mind, as in Isaiah: “It shall be month after month” [Note: [Col. 0997] 22 Isa. 66:23], because those who now rest in mind from evil will rest in future joy.

A table is the Old Testament, as in the Gospel: “The little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table” [Note: [Col. 0997] 23 Matt. 15:27], that is, the humble people of the Gentiles eat the subtlety of the Old Testament through understanding. A table, the sacred altar from which we receive the body and blood of the Lord Christ, as in Ecclesiasticus: “You have sat at a great table; carefully consider what has been set before you” [Note: [Col. 0997] 24 Sir. 31:12], that is, the sacraments of the Lord’s body and blood, which [the supplied text is corrupt] we touch upon the altar with the eye of faith. A table, sacred Scripture, as in the Psalms: “You have prepared a table before me” [Note: [Col. 0997] 25 Ps. 22:5], that is, you have made sacred Scripture humble for my understanding. A table, [lacuna] of the heavenly homeland, as in the Gospel: “That you may eat and drink at my table” [Note: [Col. 0997] 26 Luke 22:30], that is, that you may receive together the blessedness of body and soul in the heavenly homeland.

Walls are the adornments of virtues, as in Jeremiah: “He cast down all its walls” [Note: [Col. 0997] 27 Lam. 2:5], that is, he destroyed its adornments.

Midday is Christ, as in Job: “At midday they will grope as at night” [Note: [Col. 0997] 28 Job 5:14], because, just as a sinner is blind [the supplied text has the uncertain reading “sicut caecutit?”], so the Jews were blinded in the brightness of Christ. Midday, Christ’s ascension, as in the Psalms: “And at midday I will declare” [Note: [Col. 0997] 29 Ps. 55:18], that is, I will preach his [the supplied text is corrupt, perhaps “assertion”]. Midday, tribulation, as in the Song: “Where do you lie at midday?” [Note: [Col. 0997] 30 Song 1:7], that is, in what places do you rest during persecution? Midday, faith, as in Genesis [Note: [Col. 0997] 31 Gen. 18:1]: Abraham received the angels at midday, that is, in the heat of the day. Midday, sacred Scripture, as in the prophet: “We stumbled at midday” [Note: [Col. 0997] 32 Isa. 59:10], because heretics stumble in sacred Scripture through perverse understanding. Midday, the ardor of charity, as in Genesis: “At the breeze after midday” [Note: [Col. 0997] 33 Gen. 3:8], because by sin humanity had already fallen away from the charity of God.

A hired laborer is any righteous person, as in Job: “Like the days of a hired laborer are his days” [Note: [Col. 0997] 34 Job 7:1], because the righteous do not cease laboring for an eternal reward. A hired laborer, a hypocrite, as in the Gospel: “The hired laborer, whose sheep are not his own” [Note: [Col. 0997] 35 John 10:12], because the false prelate does not care for those subject to him.

A prostitute is a polluted soul, as in Isaiah: “The faithful city has become a prostitute” [Note: [Col. 0997] 36 Isa. 1:21], because the soul in which God used to dwell is polluted through sin.

The harvest is the hearer of the word of God, as in the Gospel: “The harvest indeed is great” [Note: [Col. 0997] 37 Matt. 9:37], because there are many who wish to hear, but there are not enough who might speak. The harvest, open activity, as in Job: “His harvest shall be crushed above” [Note: [Col. 0997] 38 Job 18:16], because the open activity of the impious is eventually destroyed. The harvest, the Old Testament, as in Job: “The hungry man eats the harvest of the fool” [Note: [Col. 0999] 1 Job 5:5], because the devoted people of the Gentiles understand spiritually the Old Testament, which the disgraced people of the Jews held. The harvest, the reprobate, as in the Apocalypse: “Send your sickle and reap, because the harvest of the earth is ripe” [Note: [Col. 0999] 2 Rev. 14:15], because God will cut off the reprobate with the sharpness of his judgment. The harvest, the present age, as in the Gospel: “Let both grow together until the harvest” [Note: [Col. 0999] 3 Matt. 13:30], because good and evil remain mingled together in the world until the end of the age.

Reapers are angels, as in the Gospel: “The reapers are angels” [Note: [Col. 0999] 4 Ibid., v. 39].

Crumbs are the subtleties of sacred Scripture, as in the Gospel: “Desiring to be filled with the crumbs” [Note: [Col. 0999] 5 Luke 16:21], because the people of the Gentiles desire to understand the depths of sacred Scripture.

Soldiers are angels, as in Job: “Is there any number of his soldiers?” [Note: [Col. 0999] 6 Job 25:3], because, as far as you are concerned, the angels are innumerable. Soldiers, spiritual powers, as in the Gospel: “I have soldiers under me” [Note: [Col. 0999] 7 Matt. 8:9], because the holy soul is strengthened by virtues.

Warfare is the harsh life, as in Job: “Human life is warfare upon the earth” [Note: [Col. 0999] 8 Job 7:1], because whoever lives for a long time is harassed by temptations.

A kite is the devil, as in Zechariah: “They had wings like those of a kite” [Note: [Col. 0999] 9 Zech. 5:9], because the reprobate, like the devil, raise themselves up in pride. Kites, birds of prey, as in Leviticus: “You shall not eat the kite or the vulture” [Note: [Col. 0999] 10 Lev. 11:14], that is, you must not imitate the rapacious and envious.

Myrrh is mortification, as in the Song: “My hands dripped with myrrh” [Note: [Col. 0999] 11 Song 5:5], because the workers of the holy Church devote themselves to the mortification of the flesh. Myrrh, endurance of suffering, as in the Song: “I will go to the mountain of myrrh” [Note: [Col. 0999] 12 Song 4:6], that is, by my grace I will visit those who are exalted in sufferings. Myrrh, the death of Christ, as in the Song: “My beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me” [Note: [Col. 0999] 13 Song 1:13], because Christ’s death brought the bitterness of suffering to the apostles. Myrrh, the martyrs, as in the Song: “I gathered my myrrh with my spices” [Note: [Col. 0999] 14 Song 5:1], that is, I brought my martyrs to myself.

Myrtle is moderation of thought, as in Isaiah: “Instead of the nettle the myrtle shall grow” [Note: [Col. 0999] 15 Isa. 55:13], because wherever there is prudence, there thought will be moderated. Myrtle, compassion, as in Isaiah: “The myrtle and the tree” [Note: [Col. 0999] 16 Isa. 41:19], that is, compassion and mercy.

Tamarisk is the life of the impious, as in Jeremiah: “They shall be like a tamarisk in the desert” [Note: [Col. 0999] 17 Jer. 17:6], because the life of every impious person is abandoned by God.

A mitre is steadfastness of mind, as in the book of Judith: “She bound her locks with a mitre” [Note: [Col. 0999] 18 Judith 16:10], because the faithful soul strengthens its thoughts with the firmness of steadfastness. Through a mitre [the supplied text is corrupt: “commercia”], as in Exodus: “You shall make mitres for the sons of Aaron” [Note: [Col. 0999] 19 Exod. 29:9], because the Law advises the ministers of Christ to be continent.

Moab, the Gentiles, as in the Psalms: “Moab is the pot of my hope” [Note: [Col. 0999] 20 Ps. 60:10], because the Gentile people are strengthened by hope of their salvation. Moab, any unrighteous person, as in the Psalms: “They have made a covenant against you: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites” [Note: [Col. 0999] 21 Ps. 83:6], because those who love the world, who agree with themselves in the pleasure of the flesh, and who are from the father the devil—because they are alien from the good—rise up against Christ and those who belong to Christ. For Edomites are interpreted as “earthly”; Ishmaelites, “obedient to themselves”; Moab, “from the father”; Hagar, “a foreigner.” Moab, the devil, as in Isaiah: “We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is exceedingly proud” [Note: [Col. 0999] 22 Isa. 16:6], because the devil is proud against God. Moab, sin, as in Isaiah: “Aaron has been laid waste; Moab has fallen silent” [Note: [Col. 0999] 23 Isa. 15:1], that is, once the adversary of the human race, the devil, had been destroyed through the death of Christ, the outcry of sin ceased somewhat, for “Aaron” is interpreted as “adversary.”

A bushel is temporal advantage, as in the Gospel: “They do not [the supplied text is corrupt] lower the lamp and put it under a bushel” [Note: [Col. 0999] 24 Matt. 5:15], because preaching must not be presented for temporal advantage. A bushel, perfection, as in the books of Kings: “He brought him with a bushel of flour” [Note: [Col. 0999] 25 1 Kings 1:24], because our good action must be offered to God in the perfection of inward purity.

A millstone is hope and fear, as in the Law: “You shall not take the upper or lower millstone as a pledge” [Note: [Col. 0999] 26 Deut. 24:6], because without hope and fear no one can make satisfaction for sin. A millstone, secular activity, as in Isaiah: “Take the millstone” [Note: [Col. 0999] 27 Isa. 47:2], that is, undertake secular activity. A millstone, the circuit of labors, as in the Gospel: “A millstone turned by an ass around his neck” [Note: [Col. 0999] 28 Matt. 18:6], that is, the circuit of labors in his necessity.

Through the millstone [that is, the jaw], ambushes, as in the Psalms: “He will break the jaws of the lions” [Note: [Col. 0999] 29 Ps. 59:7], that is, “the Lord” will destroy the ambushes of the cruel.

Necklaces are the instruments of virtues, as in the Song: “Your neck is like a necklace” [Note: [Col. 0999] 30 Song 1:10], that is, your preaching adorns souls. Necklaces, the flatteries of vices, as in Isaiah: “God will take away the necklaces” [Note: [Col. 0999] 31 Isa. 3:19], because he will destroy the flatteries of vices.

A mountain is the heavenly Father, as in the song of Habakkuk, where it says: “The Holy One from Mount Pharan” [Note: [Col. 0999] 32 Hab. 3:3], because Christ proceeded from the invisible Father. A mountain, Christ, as in Isaiah: “The mountain of the house of the Lord has been prepared at the summit of the mountains” [Note: [Col. 0999] 33 Isa. 2:2], because Christ, sent to the Jews, surpasses all the righteous in the sublimity of holiness. A mountain, the Church, as in the Psalms: “Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord?” [Note: [Col. 0999] 34 Ps. 24:3], that is, who [the supplied text is corrupt] reaches conformity with the Church of God? A mountain, the Jewish people, as in Isaiah: “I will sit upon the mountain of the covenant” [Note: [Col. 1001] 1 Isa. 14:13], that is, I will subject the Jewish people to myself through unbelief. A mountain, contemplation, as in Exodus: “Come up to me on the mountain” [Note: [Col. 1001] 2 Exod. 24:12], that is, touch me in some way through contemplation. A mountain, the sublimity of religion, as in Genesis: “Lot went up to Zoar and remained in the mountain” [Note: [Col. 1001] 3 Gen. 19:30], because the elect person rises from the wicked conduct of married people to the height of religion. A mountain, the heavenly homeland, as in the Psalms: “They led me to your holy mountain” [Note: [Col. 1001] 4 Ps. 43:3], that is, to that heavenly Jerusalem. A mountain, exalted righteousness, as in the Psalms: “And he heard me from his holy mountain” [Note: [Col. 1001] 5 Ps. 3:5], that is, from his lofty righteousness. A mountain, the devil, as in the Gospel: “Saying to this mountain, ‘Move from here into the sea’” [Note: [Col. 1001] 6 Matt. 17:20], because the apostles drove the ancient enemy out of the possessed and back into hell [the supplied text is fragmentary]. A mountain, a heretic, as in the Psalms: “How can you say to my soul, ‘Flee to the mountain like a sparrow’?” [Note: [Col. 1001] 7 Ps. 11:1], that is, so that [the supplied text is corrupt] may follow a heretical person, as though I could become more righteous.

A mountain, the sublimity of this world, as in Isaiah: “Raise it upon the mountain of darkness” [Note: [Col. 1001] 8 Isa. 13:2], that is, humble the world’s sublimity at the cross of Christ. A mountain, the Virgin Mary, as in Daniel: “A stone was cut from the mountain without hands” [Note: [Col. 1001] 9 Dan. 2:34], because Christ was born from Mary without male seed. Mountains signify angels, as in the Psalms: “Its foundations are upon the holy mountains” [Note: [Col. 1001] 10 Ps. 87:1], because the holy Church is founded upon the prophets. Mountains signify the apostles, as in the Psalms: “I lifted my eyes to the mountains” [Note: [Col. 1001] 11 Ps. 121:1], that is, I raised the gaze of my heart to the teaching of the apostles. Mountains signify lofty commandments, which pertain to the perfect. Mountains signify the two Testaments, as in the Psalms: “Among the midst of the mountains the waters shall pass” [Note: [Col. 1001] 12 Ps. 104:10], because streams of teaching flow in agreement between the two Testaments. Mountains signify preachers, as in the Psalms: “Let the mountains receive peace” [Note: [Col. 1001] 13 Ps. 72:3], that is, let preachers announce repentance to those subject to them [the supplied text is corrupt]. Mountains signify inner contemplations, as in Job: “He looks around the mountains of your pasture” [Note: [Col. 1001] 14 Job 39:11], that is, he considers the heights of inner contemplations in which the soul is devoutly nourished. Mountains signify proud people, as in Job: “For him the mountains bear grass” [Note: [Col. 1001] 15 Job 40:15], because the proud nourish the devil through arrogance. Mountains signify the proud hearts of the Jews, as in the books of Kings: “Mountains of Gilboa, let neither dew nor rain come upon you” [Note: [Col. 1001] 16 2 Sam. 1:21], because the proud minds of the unbelieving Jews, who killed Christ, did not receive the preaching of truth. Mountains signify the Gentiles, as in the books of Maccabees: “The sun shone upon the golden shields, and the mountains were radiant from them” [Note: [Col. 1001] 17 1 Macc. 6:39], because the Holy Spirit came to the apostles, and the Gentile peoples were illumined by them. Mountains signify evil spirits, as in the song of Habakkuk: “The everlasting mountains were shattered” [Note: [Col. 1001] 18 Hab. 3:6], because through Christ the evil spirits who are the rulers of the world were destroyed.

Death is the extinction of secular life, as in Job: “Those who await death and do not find it” [Note: [Col. 1001] 19 Job 3:21], because the saints wish to mortify themselves completely to this world, but find it. Death, pride, as in Job: “The firstborn of death will consume his arms” [Note: [Col. 1001] 20 Job 18:13], because pride, which was the first sin, will destroy the good works of the impious. Death, the devil, as in the Apocalypse: “I have the keys of death and hell,” that is, authority over the devil and his members. Death, hatred from above, as in the Psalms: “And the fear of death fell upon me” [Note: [Col. 1001] 21 Ps. 55:5], that is, I feared that hatred from above might prevail against me. Death, sin, as in the Psalms: “Lest I ever sleep in death” [Note: [Col. 1001] 22 Ps. 13:4], that is, lest I ever rest in sin. Death, eternal punishment, as in Paul: “Those who do such things are worthy of death” [Note: [Col. 1001] 23 Rom. 1:32], that is, they are worthy of eternal punishment.

A mulberry tree is the devil, as in the Gospel: “Saying to this tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea’” [Note: [Col. 1001] 24 Luke 17:6], because the apostles uprooted the devil from human beings.

A mortar is the human mind, as in the book of Numbers: “The people ground the manna in a mortar” [Note: [Col. 1001] 25 Num. 11:8], because sacred Scripture must be finely broken down in the mind through understanding. Through the mortar, martyrdoms, as in Exodus: “Mortars and censers” [Note: [Col. 1001] 26 Exod. 25:29 and 37:16], that is, martyrdoms and the hearts of the saints burning with the love of God.

A woman is the wisdom of God, as in the Gospel: “A woman having ten drachmas” [Note: [Col. 1001] 27 Luke 15:8], that is, the wisdom of God governs the divine and human creature. A woman, Christ, as in the Gospel: “A woman hid leaven in three measures of flour” [Note: [Col. 1001] 28 Matt. 13:33], because Christ divided the human race into three orders: the order of prelates, of continent persons, and of married people. A woman, the holy Church, as in Proverbs: “Who will find a strong woman?” [Note: [Col. 1001] 29 Prov. 31:10], because it belongs to God alone to establish the holy Church in the world. A woman, the Virgin Mary, as in Jeremiah: “A woman shall surround a man” [Note: [Col. 1001] 30 Jer. 31:22], that is, Mary shall conceive Christ. A woman, the human race, as in the Gospel: “And behold, a woman who had an unclean spirit” [Note: [Col. 1001] 31 Luke 13:11, 16], because the devil possessed the human race through sin. A woman, the faithful soul, as in Proverbs: “A wise woman builds her house” [Note: [Col. 1001] 32 Prov. 14:1], because the devout soul repairs its mind. A woman, the vanity of this world, as in the Apocalypse: “The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet” [Note: [Col. 1001] 33 Rev. 17:4], because lovers of this world are especially deceived through pride. A woman, cruelty, as in the Apocalypse: “I saw a woman drunk with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus” [Note: [Col. 1001] 34 Ibid., v. 6], because all the wicked, and especially cruel persecutors, delight in the mountains of Christians. A woman, heretical doctrine, as in Proverbs: “A beautiful and foolish woman” [Note: [Col. 1003] 1 Prov. 2:22], because heretical speech is beautiful because of the adornment of its words, but foolish because of the deception of its error. A woman, impiety, as in Zechariah: “And behold, a woman sitting in the middle of an ephah” [Note: [Col. 1003] 2 Zech. 5:7], because impiety rules in the mind of every reprobate. Women signify holy souls, as in the Song: “O beautiful among women” [Note: [Col. 1003] 3 Song 1:8 and 5:9, 17], that is, you who hold primacy among devout spiritual souls. Women signify subjects, as in Exodus: “Men together with women offered bracelets” [Note: [Col. 1003] 4 Exod. 35:22], because prelates, together with their subjects, offer devout actions to God. Women signify all voluptuous people, as in Isaiah: “Women shall rule over them” [Note: [Col. 1003] 5 Isa. 3:12], that is, pleasure-loving prelates shall rule over them. Woman is understood as referring to sex, as in Galatians: “Born of a woman” [Note: [Col. 1003] 6 Gal. 4:4]; and as referring to weakness, as in Job: “A man born of a woman” [Note: [Col. 1003] 7 Job 14:1].

A mule is any lazy person, as in the Psalms: “Do not become like the horse and the mule” [Note: [Col. 1003] 8 Ps. 32:9], that is, do not be proud and lazy.

Fortifications are virtues, as in Ezekiel: “And you shall build fortifications” [Note: [Col. 1003] 9 Ezek. 4:2], because the preacher ought to bring forth spiritual virtues in the heart of the subject.

A wall is Christ, as in Isaiah: “A savior will be appointed as a wall within it” [Note: [Col. 1003] 10 Isa. 26:1], because Christ is the defense of the holy Church. A wall, the Church, as in the Song: “I am a wall” [Note: [Col. 1003] 11 Song 8:10], because the holy Church fortifies those who are within it. A wall, the adversity of this world, as in the Psalms: “In my God I shall leap over a wall” [Note: [Col. 1003] 12 Ps. 18:3], that is, with God’s help I shall conquer the adversity of this world. A wall, discipline, as in Job: “When the wall was broken, they rushed upon me” [Note: [Col. 1003] 13 Job 30:14], that is, when the rigor of discipline had been destroyed, they harassed me. Walls signify the churches, as in the Song: “The guards of the walls took away my cloak” [Note: [Col. 1003] 14 Song 5:7], that is, the preachers of the churches stripped me of the evil of old age. Walls signify the virtues of the soul, as in Jeremiah: “The prince [lacuna] destroyed the walls of Jerusalem” [Note: [Col. 1003] 15 Jer. 52:14], because the vice of gluttony devastates the spiritual virtues of the soul. Walls signify the supreme rulers of the world, as in Joshua, at the sound of the trumpets: “The walls of Jericho fell” [Note: [Col. 1003] 16 Josh. 6:20], because the rulers of the world were humbled by the teaching of the preachers.

Little necklaces are the adornments of virtues, as in the Song: “We shall make golden necklaces for you” [Note: [Col. 1003] 17 Song 1:2], that is, we shall construct for you adornments of virtues full of charity.

A fly is restlessness of heart, as in Exodus: “A very grievous fly came into the houses of Pharaoh” [Note: [Col. 1003] 18 Exod. 8:24], because there is always restlessness in the mind of every reprobate.

New wine is spiritual fervor, as in the Song: “And the new wine of pomegranates” [Note: [Col. 1003] 19 Song 8:2], that is, the fervor of spiritual gifts. New wine, the vehemence of a wicked mind, as in Job: “My belly is like new wine without a vent” [Note: [Col. 1003] 20 Job 32:19], because vehemence in a perverse mind is condemned by the Holy Spirit.

A weasel is the life of the wicked, as in the Law: “You shall not eat the weasel” [Note: [Col. 1003] 21 Lev. 11:29], that is, you must not imitate the life and conduct of the wicked.

## N

Nostrils. Razor. Nest. Cloud. Grove. Nose. Cloud. Nitre. Owl. Hawk. Little boat. Spikenard. Marriage. Night. Blackness. Nerve. Night-raven. Ship. Snow.

The nostrils are Christ’s foreknowledge, as in Isaiah: “Cease from the man whose breath is in his nostrils” [Note: [Col. 1003] 22 Isa. 2:22], that is, cease provoking Christ, who in his divinity foreknows all things. Nostrils, expectation, as in Job: “The glory of his nostrils is terror” [Note: [Col. 1003] 23 Job 39:23], because holy men glory amid adversities that they know are destined to come upon them. Nostrils, folly, as in Proverbs: “A golden ring in a pig’s snout” [Note: [Col. 1003] 24 Prov. 11:22], because the speech of heretics is polished by adornment yet foolish through error. Nostrils, the devil’s instigation, as in Job: “Smoke proceeds from his nostrils” [Note: [Col. 1003] 25 Job 41:11], because the instigation of the ancient enemy generates darkness in the human mind.

Spikenard is faith, as in the Song: “Our spikenard gave forth its fragrance” [Note: [Col. 1003] 26 Song 1:12], because the faith of the holy Church manifests itself publicly. Spikenard, charity, as in the Song: “Cyprus with spikenard” [Note: [Col. 1003] 27 Song 4:13], that is, good works with charity. Spikenard, the inward sweetness of the mind, as in the Gospel [Note: [Col. 1003] 28 Mark 14:3; John 12:3], where Mary poured spikenard upon Christ’s head; that is, every believer pleases his divinity through the inward sweetness of the heart.

The nose is discernment, as in the Song: “Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon” [Note: [Col. 1003] 29 Song 7:4], because the discernment of the devout soul consists in the sublimity of holiness; for Lebanon is said to mean “whiteness.”

A ship is the Church, as in the Gospel: “He entered into one of the ships” [Note: [Col. 1003] 30 Luke 5:3], that is, into the Church, which was entrusted to Peter. A ship, the soul, as in Proverbs: “She has become like a merchant’s ship” [Note: [Col. 1003] 31 Prov. 31:14], because God, who inhabits the human soul, governs it. A ship, the human heart, as in the Gospel: “Leaving their nets and the ship, they followed him” [Note: [Col. 1003] 32 Matt. 4:20, 22; Mark 1:18], because we cannot follow Christ perfectly unless we leave behind earthly occupations and even the pleasures of our body. A ship signifies the Church throughout the world, as in the Psalms: “There the ships shall pass” [Note: [Col. 1003] 33 Ps. 104:26], because the churches have been spread throughout the entire world. Ships signify the ancient Fathers, as in Job: “Like ships carrying apples” [Note: [Col. 1003] 34 Job 9:26], because the ancient Fathers possessed, in the oracles, the sacraments of our salvation prefigured. Ships signify rulers, as in the Apocalypse: “A third of the ships perished” [Note: [Col. 1005] 1 Rev. 8:9], because those rulers who hold neither the active nor the contemplative life will perish. A ship signifies lovers of the world, as in the Psalms: “With a violent wind you will crush the ships of Tarshish” [Note: [Col. 1005] 2 Ps. 48:8], that is, in the Holy Spirit you will humble those who seek earthly joys; for Tarshish is interpreted as “seeking joy.” Ships signify the two Testaments and the peoples, as in the Gospel: “He saw two ships standing beside the shore” [Note: [Col. 1005] 3 Luke 5:2], because God knows those who are his from both.

A little boat is the Church, as in the Gospel: “So that the little boat was covered by the waves” [Note: [Col. 1005] 4 Matt. 8:24], that is, so that the Church might be harassed by tribulations. A little boat, the cross of Christ, as in the Gospel: “Jesus got into the little boat, crossed over, and came” [Note: [Col. 1005] 5 Matt. 15:39], etc., because Christ, ascending the cross, departed from the world and came to the heavenly homeland.

A cloud is ignorance, as in Job: “He spread his cloud over it” [Note: [Col. 1005] 6 Job 26:9], because even the heart of the righteous cannot, in this life, be entirely without ignorance. A cloud, the heart of any unbeliever, as in Job: “Will you raise your voice to the cloud?” [Note: [Col. 1005] 7 Job 38:34], that is, will you pour your preaching into an unbelieving heart? A cloud, the stability of the human mind, as in the books of Kings: “The priests could not stand and minister because of the cloud” [Note: [Col. 1005] 8 1 Kings 8:11], because the inner senses of the human soul cannot long serve God in a state of true uprightness, on account of the instability of wavering thoughts.

Nerve is the divine essence, as in Job: “You have set my feet in fetters” [Note: [Col. 1005] 9 Job 13:27], that is, you have bound the affection of my* mind with your strong knowledge. Nerve is the strength of the flesh, as in Genesis: “The angel touched Jacob’s thigh nerve” [Note: [Col. 1005] 10 Gen. 32:25], meaning that in a holy man inward visitation mortifies the strength of carnal pleasure. Nerve is affliction, as in Jeremiah: “He ordered him to be put in fetters” [Note: [Col. 1005] 11 Jer. 20:2], that is, to be placed in harsh affliction. By nerves are meant the virtues of the soul, as in Job: “You fitted me together with bones and nerves” [Note: [Col. 1005] 12 Job 10:11], that is, you strengthened me with powers and virtues. By nerves are meant the contrivances of the devil, as in Job: “The nerves of his testicles are intertwined” [Note: [Col. 1005] 13 Job 40:12], meaning that his devices are manifold.

Thicket is the life of the wicked, as in Judges: “Gideon destroyed * Aminadab and cut down the thicket” [Note: [Col. 1005] 14 Judg. 6:30], meaning that Christ condemns the devil’s error and the life of the wicked. Thicket is the holy Church, as in Genesis: “Abraham planted a thicket at Beersheba” [Note: [Col. 1005] 15 Gen. 21:33], and Christ established the Church in the grace of his sevenfold gift, since Beersheba is interpreted as “the seventh well.” Thicket is the splendor of secular eloquence, as when planting a thicket in the house of the Lord is forbidden [Note: [Col. 1005] 16 Deut. 16:21]: the building of the holy Church must not rest on secular splendor [Col. 1006A], and God sent Paul to evangelize not in the wisdom of speech [Note: [Col. 1005] 17 1 Cor. 2:1, 4].

Night-owl is Christ, as in the Psalms: “I have become like a night-owl * in the world” [Note: [Col. 1005] 18 Ps. 101:7], that is, I have been placed dead in the tomb.

Nest is faith, as in the Psalms: “And the turtledove has a nest for itself” [Note: [Col. 1005] 19 Ps. 83:4], meaning that the holy Church finds security in faith, in which it nourishes faithful peoples. Nest is holy conduct, as in Deuteronomy: “And the bird brooding over its young in the nest” [Note: [Col. 1005] 20 Deut. 22:6], that is, a good man persisting in good works through holy conduct. Nest is the mind of a holy man, as in Job: “And he will set his nest in high places” [Note: [Col. 1005] 21 Job 39:30], that is, he will fix his mind on heavenly things.

Little nest is simplicity, as in Job: “I shall die in my little nest” [Note: [Col. 1005] 22 Job 29:18], that is, I shall complete my days in my simplicity.

Blackness is humility, as in the Song: “His locks are like palms, black and upright” [Note: [Col. 1005] 23 Song 5:11], meaning that the raven and the angelic spirits, exalted in blessedness, were humble so that they would not fall. Blackness is outward tribulation, as in the Song: “I am black but beautiful” [Note: [Col. 1005] 24 Song 1:5], meaning that although the faithful soul is darkened by tribulation, inwardly it is beautiful before God. Blackness is a bad conscience, as in Jeremiah: “Their appearance has become blacker than coals” [Note: [Col. 1005] 25 Lam. 4:8], that is, their conscience has been darkened even more than the conscience of the wicked. Blackness is labor, as in Job: “My skin has become black upon me” [Note: [Col. 1005] 26 Job 30:30], meaning that those who serve the Church in outward activities are afflicted by labor [Col. 1006C].

Nitre is a perverse mind, as in Proverbs: “Vinegar on nitre, and one who sings a song * to a very bad heart” [Note: [Col. 1005] 27 Prov. 25:20], meaning that when a perverse mind is corrupted, it becomes worse through its corruption, just as nitre seethes and boils when vinegar is poured into it. Nitre is outward bodily cleanliness, as in Jeremiah: “Even if you wash yourself with nitre, you are not clean from the stain of sin” [Note: [Col. 1005] 28 Jer. 2:22].

Snow is a holy man, as in Jeremiah: “Her Nazirites were whiter than snow” [Note: [Col. 1005] 29 Lam. 4:7], that is, her ascetics were purer than other holy men. Snow is any sinner, as in the Psalms: “He gives snow like” [Note: [Col. 1005] 30 Ps. 147:16], meaning that he is sometimes surrounded by it as by a garment—he who was previously cold in sin [Col. 1006D]. Snow is the hearts of the nations, as in Job: “Have you entered the treasuries of * it?” [Note: [Col. 1005] 31 Job 38:22], meaning that the Lord entered the hearts of the nations. Snow is eternal damnation, as in Job: “Upon those who fear frost, snow will fall upon * it” [Note: [Col. 1005] 32 Job 6:16], meaning that those who do not wish to be afflicted for God by present tribulation are struck by eternal damnation. Snow is heavenly desire, as in Job: “If I am washed with living * waters” [Note: [Col. 1005] 33 Job 9:20], that is, if I am made clean through the compunctions of heavenly desire [Col. 1007A].

Owl is a deceitful mind, as in the Law: “You shall not eat the owl or the hawk” [Note: [Col. 1007] 1 Lev. 11:16], meaning that we must not imitate a person when he possesses a deceitful and rapacious mind.

Razor is any preacher, as in Isaiah: “God will shave the head with a hired razor, those who are beyond the river” [Note: [Col. 1007] 2 Isa. 7:20], meaning that through their preachers he cleanses the minds of those baptized in the Church from every filth of vice. Razor is any ungodly man, as in the Psalms: “You have acted deceitfully like a sharp razor” [Note: [Col. 1007] 3 Ps. 52:4], that is, [lacuna] and readily, by whatever means you can, you accomplish evil. Razor is repentance, as in the Books of Kings: “No razor shall come upon his head” [Note: [Col. 1007] 4 1 Sam. 1:11], namely, Samuel’s; meaning that in the mind of Christ there was no fleeting thought that needed to be cut away by repentance.

Night is tribulation, as in the Psalms: “Nor the moon by night” [Note: [Col. 1007] 5 Ps. 120:6], that is, the failure of virtue will not break you through tribulation. Night is the present life, as in Isaiah: “My soul desired you in the night, and my spirit also” [Note: [Col. 1007] 6 Isa. 26:9], that is, in the darkness of the present life. Night is the conduct of the laity, as in Genesis: “The greater light, to rule the day, and the lesser light, to rule the night” [Note: [Col. 1007] 7 Gen. 1:16], that is, the priestly order, which should govern the clergy, and the royal order, which should govern the crowd of laypeople. Night is the devil himself, as in the Psalms: “And night declares to night” [Note: [Col. 1007] 8 Ps. 18:3], meaning that the devil, having secretly deceived the first human being, led him to touch the tree of the knowledge of good and evil [Col. 1007C]. Night is the adversity of a holy person, as in Job: “Who gives songs in the night?” [Note: [Col. 1007] 9 Job 35:10], meaning that God consoles his elect in tribulation. Night is ignorance, as in Job: “A storm will overwhelm him by night” [Note: [Col. 1007] 10 Job 27:20], that is, ignorance will cast him down in damnation. Night is the deceiver of the human race, as in Job: “Let that night be solitary” [Note: [Col. 1007] 11 Job 3:7], that is, once the elect have been taken up for salvation, let the devil alone, together with his body—that is, the harvest of the reprobate—be condemned. Night is weakness of mind, as in Job: “And the night in which it was said, ‘A man has been conceived’” [Note: [Col. 1007] 12 Job 3:3], meaning that when the mind grows weak, it is immediately drawn into sin. Night is sin, as in Isaiah: “Watchman, what of the night?” [Note: [Col. 1007] 13 Isa. 21:11], that is: O God, what do you judge concerning my sin? By night is meant the darkness of this world, as in the Song: “On my bed, by nights, I sought him whom my soul loves” [Note: [Col. 1007] 14 Song 3:1], that is, in the present darkness I sought the Lord in my repose. By night are meant afflictions, as in the Psalms: “By night lift up your hands” [Note: [Col. 1007] 15 Ps. 133:1], that is, in afflictions raise your * actions to God [Col. 1007D].

Cloud is the Holy Spirit, as in Paul: “They were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea” [Note: [Col. 1007] 16 1 Cor. 10:2], that is, by Christ and by the Holy Spirit. Cloud is Christ’s ascension, as in the Psalms: “You who make the cloud your ascent” [Note: [Col. 1007] 17 Ps. 10:3], that is, you who ascend bodily into heaven [Col. 1008A]. Cloud is divine consolation, as in Isaiah: “A cloud by day” [Note: [Col. 1007] 18 Isa. 4:5], meaning that the Lord provides consolation through prosperity. Cloud is refreshment, as in the Apocalypse: “And they ascended into heaven in a cloud” [Note: [Col. 1007] 19 Rev. 11:12], meaning that then Enoch and Elijah will fully arrive at the kingdom, where they are in refreshment without end. Cloud is God’s protection, as in Exodus: “When Moses had gone up, the cloud covered the mountain” [Note: [Col. 1007] 20 Exod. 24:15], meaning that when someone reaches the height of contemplation, divine protection must be present to him, lest he go astray. Cloud is any holy person, as in Exodus: “They looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud” [Note: [Col. 1007] 21 Exod. 16:10], that is, they looked upon the Church, and God was seen to dwell in a holy name [Col. 1008B]. Cloud is the human flesh in Christ, as in Isaiah: “The Lord will enter Egypt, sitting upon a cloud” [Note: [Col. 1007] 22 Isa. 19:1], meaning that the Son of God entered * this world possessing human flesh free from every burden of sin. Cloud is blindness of mind, as in Ezekiel: “A storm wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud” [Note: [Col. 1007] 23 Ezek. 1:4], meaning that from the devil proceed violent temptation and blindness in the human mind. By clouds are meant preachers, as in Isaiah: “Let the clouds rain the Just One” [Note: [Col. 1007] 24 Isa. 25:8], meaning: let preachers announce Christ. By clouds is meant a prophet, as in the Psalms: “Dark water in the clouds” [Note: [Col. 1007] 25 Ps. 18:12], meaning that knowledge in the prophets is hidden. By clouds are meant the apostles, as in the Psalms: “Bringing up clouds from the end of the earth” [Note: [Col. 1007] 26 Ps. 135:7], meaning that God took not orators but fishermen as apostles. By clouds are meant the saints of the New Testament, as in Isaiah: “Who are these who fly like clouds?” [Note: [Col. 1007] 27 Isa. 60:8], meaning that the saints of the new grace rain through their words, flash through miracles, and fly in the heights through holy conduct [Col. 1008C]. By clouds are meant the wicked, as in the Epistle of Jude: “Clouds without water, carried about by winds” [Note: [Col. 1007] 28 v. 12], meaning that the wicked, lacking the moisture of grace, are driven about by temptations.

Marriage is the joys of the heavenly homeland, as in the Gospel: “When he returns from the wedding” [Note: [Col. 1007] 29 Luke 12:36], meaning that he ascended into heaven and from there will come to judge the living and the dead. Marriage is the calling of the Church, as in the Gospel: “He who made a wedding for his son” [Note: [Col. 1007] 30 Matt. 22:2], meaning that God the Father, by calling the holy Church to faith, joined it to Christ.

Daughter-in-law is the Church, as in the book of Ruth: “He has been born from your daughter-in-law, who will love you” [Note: [Col. 1007] 31 Ruth 4:15], meaning that the fruit of faith which proceeds from the Church—the deficiency of the Synagogue through true compassion *.

## O

Refined gold. Wild ass. Bone. Odor. West. [Col. 1009A] East. Orion. Eye. [Col. 1008] World. Egg. Pot. Oil. Dawn. [Col. 1009A] Nobles. Door. Olive. Midwives. Kiss. Barley. Sheep. Onocentaur. [Col. 1009A] Organ. Onycha. Sheepfold.

Refined gold is angelic dignity, as in Job: “Refined gold shall not be given for it” [Note: [Col. 1009] 1 Job 28:15], meaning that * Christ, who is the Son of God, cannot be compared even with the splendor of the angels. Refined gold is human holiness, as in Job: * “Nor have I said, ‘Refined gold is my confidence’” [Note: [Col. 1009] 2 Job 34:15], that is, I did not wish ever to place my confidence in any holiness of mine, however great it was. Refined gold is earthly wealth, as in Isaiah: “A man will be more precious than refined gold” [Note: [Col. 1009] 3 Isa. 13:12], that is, Babylon will be so destroyed that more earthly wealth than people will be found in it.

Midwives are * sinners, as in Exodus: “Because the midwives feared the Lord, he built houses for them” [Note: [Col. 1009] 4 Exod. 1:17], meaning that when those preachers themselves perfectly fear the Lord, then the people serving him increase both in merit and in number [Col. 1009B].

Eye is the intention of the heart, as in the Gospel: “If your eye is simple” [Note: [Col. 1009] 5 Matt. 6:22], that is, if your intention is pure. Eye is clarity of understanding, as in the Psalms: “My eye has been troubled by anger” [Note: [Col. 1009] 6 Ps. 30:10], that is, anger hindered my understanding. Eye is the mind of one who contemplates, as in the Psalms: “My eye has been troubled by fury” [Note: [Col. 1009] 7 Ps. 6:8], that is, my mind greatly fears your judgment when it thinks about * God. Eye is inward desire, as in Job: “My eye pours out toward the Lord” [Note: [Col. 1009] 8 Job 16:20], that is, my desire will flow toward the Lord. Eye is an intimate friend, as in the Gospel: “If your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out” [Note: [Col. 1009] 9 Matt. 18:9; Mark 9:47], that is, if your intimate friend draws you into evil, cut off his familiarity from you, lest you follow it into evil. Eye is a deed, as in the Gospel: “But you do not consider the beam in your eye” [Note: [Col. 1009] 10 Matt. 7:3; Luke 4:41], that is, you do not detect the crime in your deed. Eye is outward sight, as in the Prophet: “My eye has plundered my soul” [Note: [Col. 1009] 11 Lam. 3:51], that is, through outward inclination I rushed into sin. Eye is any preacher, as in Proverbs: “The seeing eye and the hearing ear—the Lord made both” [Note: [Col. 1009] 12 Prov. 20:12], meaning that it is by divine gift * that there is both a good teacher and a hearer. Eye is a heretic, as in Proverbs: “Let the ravens of the torrent pluck out the eye that mocks its father and despises * its mother’s portion” [Note: [Col. 1009] 13 Prov. 30:17], meaning that superiors who persist in holy teachings ought to expel from the communion of the faithful the heretic who despises Christ and the Church’s preaching. By eyes are meant the holy prophets, as in the Song: “Your eyes are like doves over streams of water” [Note: [Col. 1009] 14 Song 5:12], meaning that the holy prophets, who foresee the future, devote themselves to simplicity and sacred Scripture. By eyes are meant good preachers, as in Genesis: “His eyes are more beautiful than wine” [Note: [Col. 1009] 15 Gen. 49:12], meaning that preachers of the Gospel are superior to the teachers of the Old Testament [Col. 1010A]. By eyes are meant evil preachers, as in the Psalms: “Let their eyes be darkened” [Note: [Col. 1009] 16 Ps. 68:24], meaning that wicked teachers, because they do not wish to do what they understand, sometimes reach the point that, blinded, they do not know what they ought to do. By eyes are meant the apostles, as in the Psalms: “My eyes have failed” [Note: [Col. 1009] 17 Ps. 68:4], that is, while I trust in my Father during my Passion, my disciples fail through weakness of mind. By eyes are meant the spiritual senses, as in the Song: “Your eyes are doves” [Note: [Col. 1009] 18 Song 4:1], meaning that the inward senses of the devout soul attend to simplicity. By eyes are meant the teachers of the Jews, as in Jeremiah: “Their eyes failed, because there was no grass” [Note: [Col. 1009] 19 Jer. 14:6], that is, the teachers vanished because they did not possess the inward verdure of hope. By eyes are meant the counselors of the devil, as in Job: “His eyes are like the eyelids of dawn” [Note: [Col. 1009] 20 Job 41:9], meaning that Satan’s counselors draw their hearers into darkness while pretending to pour clarity into them. By eyes are meant the preachers of Antichrist, as in Job: “My enemy has looked upon me with terrifying eyes” [Note: [Col. 1009] 21 Job 16:9], meaning that the devil will greatly terrify the holy Church through the preachers of Antichrist. By eyes are meant illicit desires, as in Genesis: “The eyes of both were opened” [Note: [Col. 1009] 22 Gen. 3:7], meaning that after sin there were illicit desires in the human soul toward earthly things against the Lord. By eyes are meant thoughts, as in Job: “Whoever lowers his eyes will not be saved” [Note: [Col. 1009] 23 Job 22:29], and whoever humbles the thoughts of his mind will attain true salvation. By eyes are meant proud movements of the heart, as in Job: “As though thinking great thoughts, you have astonished the eyes” [Note: [Col. 1009] 24 Job 15:12], that is, as though you were considering lofty things about yourself, you are proud in your mind [Col. 1010C]. By eyes are meant harsher looks, as in Job: “I made a covenant with my eyes, not to think about a virgin” [Note: [Col. 1009] 25 Job 31:1], that is, I restrained my outward action from vanity, lest I be drawn to think about her. By eyes are meant peoples, as in the Song: “You have wounded my heart with one of your eyes” [Note: [Col. 1009] 26 Song 4:9], that is, O Church, you have drawn me to delight through the unanimity of your peoples.

West is decrepit old age, as in the Gospel: “Many will come from the West” [Note: [Col. 1009] 27 Matt. 8:11; Luke 13:29], that is, many will attain holiness in decrepit old age. West is unbelief, as in the Apocalypse: “From the west, three gates” [Note: [Col. 1009] 28 Rev. 21:13], meaning that those who are in a failure of faith sometimes come to faith in the Trinity. West is the failure of virtue, as in Job: “If I go toward the west, I shall not understand him” [Note: [Col. 1009] 29 Job 23:8], meaning that those who fall from virtue through the lapse of sin by no means understand God purely.

Odor is the sweetness of holiness, as in the Song: “And the fragrance of your perfumes surpasses all spices” [Note: [Col. 1009] 30 Song 4:10], that is, the sweetness of your virtues surpasses all the pleasant things of this life. Odor is a good life, as in the Song: “And the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of incense” [Note: [Col. 1009] 31 Ibid. v. 11], that is, the good reputation of your works displays the devotion that you possess in prayer [Col. 1011A]. Odor is holiness of speech, as in the Song: “The fragrance of your mouth is like apples” [Note: [Col. 1011] 1 Song 7:8], that is, you are as holy in speech as you are in action.

Olive is mercy, as in Isaiah: “Myrtle and wood of olives” [Note: [Col. 1011] 2 Isa. 41:19], that is, compassion and the virtue of mercy. Olive is the Holy Spirit, as in the Book of Judges: “The olives said, ‘Rule over us’” [Note: [Col. 1011] 3 Judg. 9:8], meaning that those who cannot fruitfully possess the Spirit by faith do not wish to accept that that olive will rule. Olive is the works of the righteous, as in the Psalms: “But I am like a fruitful olive tree” [Note: [Col. 1011] 4 Ps. 51:2], that is, I lived in the likeness of the righteous who came before. Olive is any hypocrite, as in Job: “Like an olive tree casting off its blossom” [Note: [Col. 1011] 5 Job 15:33], meaning that the hypocrite sometimes loses the appearance of outward holiness that he seems to possess [Col. 1011B]. Olive is the Jewish people, as in the Song of Habakkuk: “The work of the olive will fail” [Note: [Col. 1011] 6 Hab. 3:17], meaning that the legal observance which the Jews possessed has now ceased.

Oil is the Holy Spirit, as in Isaiah: “The yoke will rot before the oil” [Note: [Col. 1011] 7 Isa. 10:27], that is, sin will fail in the presence of the Holy Spirit. Oil is inward grace, as in Job: “The rock poured out streams of oil for me” [Note: [Col. 1011] 8 Job 29:6], that is, Christ bestowed on me the gifts of his grace. Oil is devotion of mind, as in Exodus: “Let them bring you pure oil from the trees” [Note: [Col. 1011] 9 Exod. 27:20], meaning that, following the examples of the fathers who came before, we ought to offer God [lacuna] devotion. Oil is charity, as in Ecclesiastes: “Let oil not fail from your head” [Note: [Col. 1011] 10 Eccl. 9:8], that is, let charity always endure in your mind. Oil is the testimony of the heart, as in the Gospel: “But the wise took oil in their vessels” [Note: [Col. 1011] 11 Matt. 25:4], meaning that holy men possess the testimony of conscience in their hearts. Oil is consolation, as in the Gospel: “Pouring in oil and wine” [Note: [Col. 1011] 12 Luke 10:34], that is, consolation and correction. Oil is the fame of divine praise, as in the Song: “Oil poured out is your name” [Note: [Col. 1011] 13 Song 1:3], meaning that the excellence of divine praise is celebrated in the Church. Oil is any active person, as in the Apocalypse: “Do not harm the oil and the wine” [Note: [Col. 1011] 14 Rev. 6:6], that is, you will not distinguish between contemplatives and active people. Oil is flattery, as in the Psalms: “But may the oil of the sinner not anoint my head” [Note: [Col. 1011] 15 Ps. 140:5], that is, may the favor of the flatterer not gladden my heart.

Pot is tribulation, as in the Psalms: “Moab is the pot of my hope” [Note: [Col. 1011] 16 Ps. 59:10], that is, the tribulation that I suffer from the devil increases me in hope [Col. 1011D]. Pot is a reprobate mind, as in Jeremiah: “I see a boiling pot” [Note: [Col. 1011] 17 Jer. 1:13], that is, I see a reprobate mind inflamed by carnal desires. Pot is the malice of the devil, as in Job: “The deep sea boils like a pot” [Note: [Col. 1011] 18 Job 41:22], meaning that the devil, following the example of his own malice, sets the perverse heart ablaze.

Onocentaur is any reprobate and lustful person, as in Isaiah: “Demons will meet onocentaurs” [Note: [Col. 1011] 19 Isa. 34:14], meaning that demons delight in those who are proud and slippery, since ὄνος means “ass,” through which lust is expressed, and it is commonly understood * through the bull [Col. 1012A].

Wild ass is Christ, as in Job: “Who has set the wild ass free?” [Note: [Col. 1011] 20 Job 39:8], meaning that through Christ God freed humanity from the captivity of mortality. Wild ass means the Gentiles, as in Job: “Will the wild ass bray when it has * no prey?” [Note: [Col. 1011] 21 Job 6:5], meaning that the Gentile people were freed from their deadly grief when they came to know Christ through faith. By the wild ass are meant the Jewish people, as in the Psalms: “The wild asses will wait in their thirst” [Note: [Col. 1011] 22 Ps. 109:11], meaning that now the Jews await their salvation with great desire, because * the remnant will be saved. By the wild ass are meant heretics, as in Job: “Like wild asses they go out to their work in the desert” [Note: [Col. 1011] 23 Job 24:5], meaning that heretics burst into the Church to lead the faithful people astray [Col. 1012B].

Onycha is prayer, as in Exodus: “Onycha and galbanum * for a man’s fragrance” [Note: [Col. 1011] 24 Exod. 30:34], that is, prayer and the practice of good repute.

Nobles are teachers, as in Job: “And he overthrows nobles” [Note: [Col. 1011] 25 Job 12:19], meaning that God drives away from himself proud teachers.

World is this world, as in Job: “Under it those who bear up the world are bent down” [Note: [Col. 1011] 26 Job 9:13], meaning that even the angels who govern this world are humbled in contemplation of the divine majesty. World is the Church, as in the Song: “And he set the world upon them” [Note: [Col. 1011] 27 1 Sam. 2:8], meaning that God keeps his elect written in the book of blessed predestination [Col. 1012C].

Barley is action, as in Job: “Let a thorn spring up for me instead of barley” [Note: [Col. 1011] 28 Job 31:30], that is, in me let the prick of sin take the place of strong action. Barley is the Old Testament, as in the Gospel: “A boy who had five barley loaves” [Note: [Col. 1011] 29 John 6:9], meaning that the people, childish in understanding, possessed the old Law contained in the five books of Moses.

Organ is joy of mind, as in Job: “And my organ into the voice of weeping” [Note: [Col. 1011] 30 Job 30:31], that is, I who used to rejoice am now full of sorrow. By the organ are meant preachings, as in the Psalms: “Upon the willows in its midst we hung our organs” [Note: [Col. 1011] 31 Ps. 136:2], that is, before the proud and fruitless, who persist in the confusion of vices, we do not wish to display our preachings [Col. 1012D].

Dawn is Christ, as * in Zechariah: “The dawn from on high has visited us” [Note: [Col. 1011] 32 Luke 1:78], that is, Christ came to us from heaven. Dawn is childhood, as in the Gospel: “Many will come from the east” [Note: [Col. 1011] 33 Matt. 8:11], meaning that many come to Christ from childhood. Dawn is the Jewish people, as in the Apocalypse: “From the east, three gates” [Note: [Col. 1011] 34 Rev. 21:13], meaning that the faithful city was announced to the * Jews. Dawn is holiness of life, as in Job [Note: [Col. 1011] 35 Job 23:8]: “If I go from the east, he does not appear” [Col. 1013A], that is, although I may be holy in life, I am nevertheless not fully secure.

Orions are martyrs, as in Job: “He who made Arcturus and Orion” [Note: [Col. 1013] 1 Job 9:9], meaning that God founded the holy Church and produced holy martyrs in it.

Garden is the holy Church, as in the Song: “A garden enclosed is my sister, my bride” [Note: [Col. 1013] 2 Song 4:12], meaning that the holy Church is fortified on every side by living faith. Garden is a holy mind, as in the Song: “Let my beloved come into his garden” [Note: [Col. 1013] 3 Ibid. 5:16], that is, let him visit my mind, in which he planted the shoots of his graces. Garden is the heavenly homeland, as in the Song: “I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride” [Note: [Col. 1013] 4 Song 5:1], that is, hasten to come to the heavenly homeland, where I am. Garden is the faithful soul *. Garden is pleasure, as in the Books of Kings: “Give me your vineyard, so that I may make myself a garden of vegetables” [Note: [Col. 1013] 5 1 Kings 21:2], meaning that the devil wishes to transfer a person’s spiritual joy into the pleasure of carnal desires [Col. 1013B].

Mouth is the Son of God, as in Job: “And the sound proceeding from his mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 6 Job 37:2], that is, the instruction of the supreme Father * concerning the Son. Mouth is any preacher, as in the Apocalypse: “I am about to vomit you out of my mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 7 Rev. 3:16], that is, through my preachers I will cast you out from the company of the saints. Mouth is the secret of a good mind, as in the Psalms: “And my mouth will proclaim your praise” [Note: [Col. 1013] 8 Ps. 50:17], that is, in the secret place of my mind I will praise you. Mouth is an evil thought, as in Job: “For when evil is sweet in his mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 9 Job 20:12], that is, when sin is pleasant to him in thought. Mouth is speech, as in Job: “I will put my hand over my mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 10 Job 40:4], that is, through good action I will correct whatever I have done wrong through evil speech [Col. 1013C]. Mouth is a great sin, as in Job: “He will save you from the narrow mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 11 Job 36:16], that is, * I will free you from the great sin in which you are confined by darkness. Mouth is the devil’s cunning, as in Job: “He will save you from the narrow mouth, and who has entered into the midst of his mouth?” [Note: [Col. 1013] 12 Job 41:4], that is, who but I has fully exposed the devil’s cunning?

Bone—of bone—is strength of mind, as in the Psalms: “There is no bone [lacuna]”, that is, if there is any strength in me, it is not unknown to you. Bone is Christ’s divinity, as in Exodus: “You shall not * break a bone of it” [Note: [Col. 1013] 13 Exod. 12:46], meaning that they could not kill the divinity in Christ. Bone is the strength of Christ’s Passion, as in Job: “My bone has clung to my skin after my flesh was consumed” [Note: [Col. 1013] 14 Job 19:20], that is, in the harshness of my Passion, while my disciples fled, the women who ought to have been closer stood by. By bones are meant the virtues of the soul, as in Job: “He makes all his bones wither” [Note: [Col. 1013] 15 Job 33:19], that is, he permits his virtues to fail. By bones are meant strong deeds, as in Job: “All my bones were terrified” [Note: [Col. 1013] 16 Job 4:14], that is, I placed no confidence in any of my strong works. By bones is meant the strength of the flesh, as in Job: “And my bones [to] death” [Note: [Col. 1013] 17 Job 7:15], that is, the strength of my flesh has failed. By bones are meant evil habits, as in Job: “And his bones are moistened with marrow” [Note: [Col. 1013] 18 Job 21:24], that is, the evil habits of the wicked are renewed by carnal pleasures. By bones are meant the devil’s suggestions, as in Job: “His bones are like tubes of bronze” [Note: [Col. 1013] 19 Job 40:13], meaning that the devil’s suggestions, while they sound soothing, deceive him. By bones is meant evil doctrine, as in Jeremiah: “Their skin has clung to their bones” [Note: [Col. 1013] 20 Lam. 4:8], that is, their softness has been changed into * hardness [Col. 1014A].

Kiss is the gift of the Holy Spirit, as in the Song: “Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth” [Note: [Col. 1013] 21 Song 1:1], that is, let him adorn me with the gift of the Holy Spirit. Kiss is charity, as in the Gospel: “You did not give me a kiss” [Note: [Col. 1013] 22 Luke 7:45], meaning that the Jewish people did not wish to serve God through charity. By a kiss are meant deceptions, as in Proverbs: “Better are the wounds of a friend than the deceitful kisses of an enemy” [Note: [Col. 1013] 23 Prov. 27:6], meaning that a friend’s corrections are more useful than an enemy’s deceptions [Col. 1014B].

Door is Christ, as in the Gospel: “I am the door of the sheep” [Note: [Col. 1013] 24 John 10:7], meaning that through Christ the faithful enter the kingdom. Door is the opening in Christ’s side, as in the Books of Kings: “The door of the middle side” [Note: [Col. 1013] 25 1 Kings 6:8], which was in the right part of the house; this was the Lord’s open side, from which the sacraments of our salvation flowed forth. Door is the Church, as in the Song: “If it is a door, let us panel * it with cedar boards” [Note: [Col. 1013] 26 Song 8:9], that is, we will adorn the holy Church, through which entry to the heavenly homeland lies open, with holy men. Door is contemplatives, as in Ezekiel, * in an inward vision. Door is our mouth, as in Job: “I was silent and did not go out through the door” [Note: [Col. 1013] 27 Job 31:34], that is, I did not go out by speaking through my mouth. Door is understanding of the word of God, as in the Gospel: “The door is already shut” [Note: [Col. 1013] 28 Luke 11:7], that is, understanding of the word is not open. Door is the order of hearers, as in the Apocalypse: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock” [Note: [Col. 1013] 29 Rev. 3:20], that is, I rouse the heart so that it may be opened. Door is entry into the heavenly kingdom, as in Exodus: “The Lord shall offer him to the gods, and he shall be brought to the door” [Note: [Col. 1013] 30 Exod. 21:6], that is, he will be subjected to the [lacuna] and compelled by them, so that he may be worthy to enter the heavenly kingdom. By the door are meant holy preachers, as in Job: “And I set bars and doors” [Note: [Col. 1013] 31 Job 38:10], meaning that God the Father sent Christ and preachers to restrain the world. By the door are meant love of God and neighbor, according to the examples of the holy Fathers. By the door are meant carnal desires, as in Job: “He did not close the doors of the womb that carried me” [Note: [Col. 1013] 32 Job 3:10], that is, he did not avoid the desires of pleasure, who exposed me to sin. By doors are meant evil spirits, as in Job: “And you saw the dark doors” [Note: [Col. 1013] 33 Job 38:17], meaning that, while dying, the Lord conquered the evil spirits whose suggestions the reprobate obey and through whom they find an entrance to eternal death [Col. 1014D].

Egg is hope, as in the Gospel: “Or if he asks for an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?” [Note: [Col. 1013] 34 Luke 11:12], meaning that when we ask hope from * God, he will certainly not give us despair. By eggs are meant subjects, as in Job: “Which leaves its eggs on the ground” [Note: [Col. 1015] 1 Job 39:17], meaning that an evil prelate permits his subjects to engage in earthly works alien to true religion. By eggs are meant the counsels of demons, as in Isaiah: “Whoever eats of the eggs of asps will die” [Note: [Col. 1015] 2 Isa. 59:5], meaning that whoever consents to the suggestions of demons incurs the death of his soul.

The sheep signifies innocence, as in Job: “They each gave him one sheep of their own [Note: [Col. 1015] 3 Job 42:11],” meaning that all who belong to Christ strive to offer him the virtue of innocence in the unity of charity. The sheep signifies Christ, as in Isaiah: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter [Note: [Col. 1015] 4 Isa. 53:7],” meaning that the innocent Christ was punished by death. The sheep signifies the redeemed human being, as in the Gospel: “I have found the sheep that I had lost [Note: [Col. 1015] 5 Luke 15:6],” meaning that by dying Christ found the human being lost through sin. Sheep signify angels, as in the Gospel: “He leaves the ninety-nine sheep in the wilderness [Note: [Col. 1015] 6 ibid., v. 4],” meaning that Christ left the angels in heaven when he sought the lost human being in the world. Sheep signify faithful peoples, as in Ezekiel: “Behold, I myself will feed my sheep [Note: [Col. 1015] 7 Ezek. 34:15],” meaning that Christ spiritually refreshes his faithful*. Sheep signify pure thoughts, as in Job: “The fire of God fell from heaven and consumed the sheep and the servants [Note: [Col. 1015] 8 Job 1:16],” meaning that pure thoughts in a human being are sometimes, by God’s permission, burned up by the heat of lust. Sheep signify reprobate human beings, as in the Psalms: “Like sheep they have been placed in hell [Note: [Col. 1015] 9 Ps. 48:15],” meaning that the reprobate perish in their folly. Sheep signify good subjects, as in Genesis: “The sheep gave birth to various offspring [Note: [Col. 1015] 10 Gen. 31:8],” that is, good subjects displayed a variety of good actions. Sheep signify wanton movements of the mind, as in Leviticus: “If the offering is from *all [Note: [Col. 1015] 11 Lev. 3:6],” meaning that we ought to slaughter the movements of wantonness within us through the cultivation of *maturity. Sheep signify David’s wives, as Bathsheba, Uriah’s wife, signifies a sheep, as in the Books of Kings: “Sparing to take from his own sheep, he took the poor man’s sheep and prepared a banquet for the stranger who had come to him [Note: [Col. 1015] 12 2 Sam. 12:4],” meaning that David then, setting aside his own wives, seized Uriah’s wife to satisfy the desire of his lust, which had tempted him.

The sheepfold signifies the Synagogue, as in the Gospel: “I have other sheep that are not from this sheepfold [Note: [Col. 1015] 13 John 10:6],” that is, the Gentiles, who do not belong to the Synagogue; and in the Song of Habakkuk: “The flock shall be cut off from the sheepfold [Note: [Col. 1015] 14 Hab. 3:17],” meaning that the heretic shall be cut off from the Church.

## P

[Col. 1015D]

Peace. Fish. Foot. Eyelids. Portico. Little wings. Sole of the foot. Defender. Prey. Papyrus. Bar. Little breast. [Col. 1016A] Pool. Sin. Cloak. Gate. Feather. Pasture. Lead. Pine. [text uncertain: *Pedus]. Hairs. Father. Point. Prince. Well. Dwarf. Peliades. [Col. 1015D] Fruits. Fortifications. Manger. Wall. Paintings. Cattle. Vine-shoot. High priest. Plaits. [text uncertain: *Palvicus]. Painter. Stranger. [Col. 1016A] Stake. Orphan. Sparrow. Feather. Wound. Mercy seat. Partridge. Cloths. Child. Leopard. Peaceful. Fishermen. Skin. Pores. Melons. Plane trees. [Col. 1015D] Bread. Paradise. Powerful ones. Dust. Pelican. Marshes. Pigs. Bag. Street. Posts. Robbers. Chick. [Col. 1016A] Firstborn. Hairy ones. Floor. Pupil of the eye. Frost. Feather. Pylades. Sparrow. Prince. Hairs. Father. Plaits. [text uncertain: *Palvicus]. Chick. Frost.

Peace signifies Christ, as in Paul: “He himself is our peace, who made both one [Note: [Col. 1015] 15 Eph. 2:14],” meaning that Christ joined human nature to angelic nature in one blessedness, and some of the Jews and many of the Gentiles in one fellowship. Peace signifies social love: “Have salt in yourselves, and peace among yourselves [Note: [Col. 1015] 16 Mark 9:50],” that is, possess such confidence within yourselves that you do not neglect to have love toward the simple. Peace signifies repose of mind, as in the Psalms: “And his dwelling became a place of peace [Note: [Col. 1015] 17 Ps. 75:3],” meaning that God dwells in a prepared and peaceful mind. Peace signifies the tranquility of contemplation, as in the Psalms: “In peace, in the same place, I shall sleep [Note: [Col. 1015] 18 Ps. 4:9],” that is, in the tranquility of contemplation and unity of spirit I possess rest. Peace signifies the redemption of the human race, as in Isaiah: “The feet of the one announcing and preaching peace [Note: [Col. 1015] 19 Isa. 52:7],” that is, the affections of any prophet announcing the redemption of humanity. Peace signifies preaching, as in the Psalms: “Let the mountains receive peace for the people [Note: [Col. 1015] 20 Ps. 71:3],” that is, let the apostles receive the preaching that they are to proclaim to the world. Peace signifies repentance, as in Paul: “He announced peace to those who were far away [Note: [Col. 1015] 21 Eph. 2:17],” meaning that Christ preached repentance both to the faithful Jews and to the unbelieving Gentiles. Peace signifies future rest, as in the Book of Joshua: “Peace was given to him from all the nations round about [Note: [Col. 1015] 22 Josh. 21:44],” meaning that in the future the elect will have no disturbance whatsoever from any enemy, but complete peace in every respect. Peace signifies carnal agreement, as in the Gospel: “I did not come to bring peace, but a sword [Note: [Col. 1015] 23 Matt. 10:34],” that is, I do not wish to foster softness in the flesh, but separation from the flesh.

There is disordered peace, simulated peace, defiled peace, and criminal peace. The first belongs to the proud, who, despising the one above them, obey the one below them: despising God, they obey the devil; despising heaven, they obey the world; despising the spirit, they obey the flesh. The second belongs to the double-minded, who, meditating wickedness in their hearts, possessing deceitful lips, and speaking with “a heart and a heart,” blessed with their mouths and cursed in their hearts. The third belongs to the unclean, who, shamefully prostituted, rest, satisfied with their filth. The fourth belongs to rebels and schismatics, who resist social love and oppose the authority of the whole Church.

Peaceful signifies Christ, as in the Song: “The vineyard belonged to the peaceful one [Note: [Col. 1017] 1 Song 8:11],” meaning that through the Law Christ cultivated the Synagogue. Peaceful signifies any holy person, as in the Psalms: “With those who hated peace I was peaceful [Note: [Col. 1017] 2 Ps. 119:7],” meaning that holy men possess serenity of mind not only toward friends but also toward enemies. Peaceful ones signify preachers, as in the Song: “A thousand are your peaceful ones [Note: [Col. 1017] 3 Song 8:12],” meaning that holy preachers who announce peace to the Church possess the perfection of virtue, since the number one thousand is perfect. Peaceful ones signify lovers of concord, as in the Gospel: “God’s peaceful ones,” that is, lovers of concord, “for they shall be called children of God [Note: [Col. 1017] 4 Matt. 5:9].”

The palm signifies the Church, as in Job: “And like a palm tree I shall multiply my days [Note: [Col. 1017] 5 Job 29:18],” meaning that the holy Church produces increases of understanding and inward illumination in holy men. The palm signifies the just person, as in the Psalms: “The just shall flourish like a palm tree [Note: [Col. 1017] 6 Ps. 92:13],” meaning that the holy man strives to conform himself in the radiance of righteousness to the prayers that have gone before him. The palm signifies the holy cross, as in the Song: “I shall climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruits [Note: [Col. 1017] 7 Song 7:8],” that is, I shall contemplate the power of the cross and strive to share in its reward. The palm signifies right intention, as in the Song: “Your stature is like a palm tree [Note: [Col. 1017] 8 ibid., 5:7],” that is, in your outward good action it appears how upright your intention is.
